items.followUp: State one chemical property of metal oxides.

rubric.why: Identifies the general nature of metal oxides.
rubric.description: Metal oxides are generally basic in nature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that metal oxides are basic or alkaline.

rubric.why: Gives a characteristic reaction that supports their basic nature.
rubric.description: A metal oxide reacts with an acid to form salt and water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the reaction products: salt and water.

modelAnswer: Metal oxides are generally basic in nature.
They react with acids to form salt and water.

items.followUp: Describe how electronegativity changes across a period and down a group.

rubric.why: States the trend down a group.
rubric.description: Electropositivity increases down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct down-group trend.

rubric.why: States the trend across a period.
rubric.description: Electropositivity decreases from left to right across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct across-period trend.

modelAnswer: Electropositivity increases down a group in the periodic table.
It decreases from left to right across a period.

items.followUp: Define valency and explain how an atom can acquire a negative valency.

rubric.why: Defines an element as a substance made of one kind of atom.
rubric.description: An element is a pure substance composed of only one kind of atom.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the idea that an element contains only one kind of atom.

rubric.why: States what valency means.
rubric.description: Valency is the combining capacity of an atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining valency as combining capacity.

rubric.why: Explains how positive valency arises.
rubric.description: An atom has positive valency when it loses electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking electron loss with positive valency.

rubric.why: Explains how negative valency arises.
rubric.description: An atom has negative valency when it gains electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking electron gain with negative valency.

modelAnswer: An element is a pure substance composed of only one kind of atom.
Valency is the combining capacity of an atom.
An atom has positive valency when it loses electrons.
An atom has negative valency when it gains electrons.

items.followUp: What are isotopes? Give two uses of isotopes.

rubric.why: Defines isotopes using their atomic and mass numbers or their subatomic particles.
rubric.description: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that isotopes have the same number of protons and different numbers of neutrons, or the equivalent atomic- and mass-number definition.

rubric.why: Names a valid use of a radioactive isotope.
rubric.description: Carbon-14 is used to determine the age of fossils or archaeological remains.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for carbon-14 dating.

rubric.why: Names a valid medical use of an isotope.
rubric.description: Cobalt-60 is used in the treatment of cancer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for cobalt-60 cancer treatment or radiotherapy.

rubric.why: Names another valid use of an isotope.
rubric.description: Iodine-131 is used to diagnose or treat thyroid disorders; uranium-235 is used as nuclear fuel.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either valid use.

modelAnswer: Isotopes are atoms of the same element having the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
Carbon-14 is used to determine the age of fossils and archaeological remains.
Cobalt-60 is used in the treatment of cancer.
Iodine-131 is used to diagnose or treat thyroid disorders.

items.followUp: Define evaporation and explain how humidity and wind speed affect it.

rubric.why: Defines evaporation as a surface process in which a liquid changes to vapour.
rubric.description: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the liquid-to-vapour change occurring at the surface.

rubric.why: Explains the effect of exposed surface area.
rubric.description: Increasing the surface area increases the rate of evaporation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a larger surface area increases evaporation.

rubric.why: Explains the effect of temperature.
rubric.description: Increasing the temperature increases the rate of evaporation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that higher temperature increases evaporation.

rubric.why: Explains the effects of humidity and moving air.
rubric.description: Low humidity and higher wind speed increase the rate of evaporation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly explaining either factor.

modelAnswer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface.
A larger exposed surface area increases the rate of evaporation.
Higher temperature increases the rate of evaporation.
Low humidity increases evaporation, while higher wind speed carries vapour away and increases evaporation.

items.followUp: Write four characteristics of a solution.

rubric.why: Identifies the non-uniform nature of a suspension.
rubric.description: A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as heterogeneous.

rubric.why: States that suspension particles are large enough to be seen.
rubric.description: Its particles are large enough to be visible.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the particles can be seen.

rubric.why: States that suspension particles settle when left undisturbed.
rubric.description: The particles settle down on standing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that particles settle on standing.

rubric.why: States a method for separating suspension particles.
rubric.description: The particles can be separated from the mixture by filtration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a suspension can be separated by filtration.

modelAnswer: A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.
Its particles are large enough to be seen.
The particles settle down when the suspension is left standing.
The particles can be separated from the mixture by filtration.

items.followUp: Define variable valency and give an example of an element that shows it.

rubric.why: Defines variable valency as the ability to show more than one valency.
rubric.description: Variable valency is the property of an element to show more than one valency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an element can have different valencies.

rubric.why: Provides a correct example and its valencies.
rubric.description: For example, iron has valencies of 2 and 3.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid element with two stated valencies.

modelAnswer: Variable valency is the property of an element to show more than one valency.
For example, iron has valencies of 2 and 3.

items.followUp: Define formula mass and calculate the formula mass of CO₂.

rubric.why: Defines formula mass as the sum of the atomic masses represented in a formula.
rubric.description: Formula mass is the sum of the atomic masses of all atoms in a chemical formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the sum-of-atomic-masses definition.

rubric.why: Gives a correct example and calculated formula mass.
rubric.description: For H₂O, the formula mass is 2(1) + 16 = 18 u.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example with its formula mass.

modelAnswer: Formula mass is the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms represented in a chemical formula.
For example, formula mass of H₂O = 2(1) + 16 = 18 u.
